reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a flash-loan arbitrage smart contract while claiming that FTM can be multiplied by more than 400. It instructs viewers to connect MetaMask, deploy the contract, confirm transactions, and send 98 FTM, with another transfer suggested if the process fails. The stated return and visible wallet screens do not independently verify the contract's behavior, profit source, or recoverability of funds.

Send FTM to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 98 FTM
Now I need to supply this contract slash coin with enough gas to be able to arbitrage trade back and forth with itself.
I'll make it 98 FTM that I'm gonna send to the contract.
At the start, we only made like 1200

opening.argument: This is framed as a risk-aware technical exercise, not an unconditional financial promise. The accompanying material expressly warns that flash-loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable protocols and steal millions, and the on-screen document says “This is for educational purposes only” and “Try at your own risk.” The underlying mechanism is also described as requiring repayment within the same transaction, which highlights a technical constraint rather than passive or guaranteed income. Those warnings make the presentation materially different from a concealed solicitation: viewers are told the activity is experimental and risky, while the video explains the mechanics for educational use.

citations.quote: flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and steal millions of dollars
A flash loan has to be borrowed and repaid within the same blockchain transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument treats the presence of operational steps as proof of deception, but it omits the explicit educational and risk language. Sending funds is described as supplying gas for the arbitrage process, not as a fee paid to the presenter, and the supplied material does not establish that the presenter receives or controls viewers’ funds. A demonstrated transaction and an ambitious title may warrant caution, but they do not by themselves negate the stated warnings or prove a guaranteed outcome.

citations.quote: Now I need to supply this contract slash coin with enough gas to be able to arbitrage trade back and forth with itself.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not cure the central inducement. The material still tells viewers to deploy a contract and send FTM to it, while the title promises multiplication of more than 400. Calling the transfer gas describes its alleged purpose, not whether the contract is trustworthy or whether funds can be recovered. “Educational” and “at your own risk” disclaimers therefore qualify the presentation but do not remove its concrete invitation to fund the process.

opening.argument: The video is best understood as an operational programming demonstration. The speaker walks through creating a Remix workspace, naming the Solidity file, pasting source code, selecting compiler version 0.5.16, connecting MetaMask through injected Web3, deploying a contract, and then executing the flash loan. The description likewise presents a numbered step-by-step tutorial. The focus is on how blockchain tooling, contracts, wallets, and atomic loans interact; the speaker is showing a process on screen rather than merely asserting that viewers will receive money. A claimed personal result is evidence of what the demonstrator says happened, not certification that every viewer will obtain the same result.

You're going to go injected web 3, make sure. Meta mask and everything connects up.
Step By Step Tutorial for Flash Loan

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of instructions does not turn a technical demonstration into a financial solicitation. The narration explains deployment, compiler configuration, and wallet connection in concrete software terms, and the video visibly shows development tooling and transaction controls. The opposing reading relies heavily on the title and one reported result, but a tutorial can document a personal experiment without independently guaranteeing its repeatability. The technical subject remains the dominant context.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial format is precisely what makes the content actionable: it supplies the code workflow, wallet connection, deployment sequence, funding amount, and execution step. The speaker does not merely study software; he says the process generates profits and calls it easy and fast. Technical presentation style cannot erase the financial solicitation created by those instructions and the promised result.

opening.argument: The described transaction resembles an ordinary software-and-service workflow: a user configures a wallet, deploys a contract, supplies network gas, and uses decentralized exchanges for a token swap. The speaker specifically characterizes the 98 FTM as gas needed to run the arbitrage, rather than a membership payment or transfer to a recruiter. The supplied material shows no downline, referral compensation, credential request, or promise that the presenter will manage deposits. It also explains that the loan must be borrowed and repaid in one transaction. On this record, the content describes interacting with public blockchain tools and an exchange mechanism, while the safety of that external code remains something users must assess themselves.

citations.quote: With the gas we need to run the arbitrage.
Then we're going to get a flash loan to trade that against Zootre.
A flash loan has to be borrowed and repaid within the same blockchain transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account labels the workflow a deposit mechanism without showing that the funds go to the presenter or that a return is guaranteed. The narration identifies the transfer as operational gas, and the visible interface is a wallet and contract-development environment. A user-funded transaction can be risky without being a scam, especially where the material describes exchange execution and an atomic loan rather than recruitment or credential collection.

citations.quote: enough gas to be able to arbitrage trade back and forth with itself.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the transfer gas does not make it an ordinary purchase or establish that the contract will perform as claimed. The instructions specifically require sending 98 FTM and suggest sending another 100 FMT if the process fails, while the title advertises multiplying FTM 400+. The absence of a downline or password request is beside the point: the relevant mechanism is inducing viewers to fund a contract on the strength of extraordinary returns that are not independently verified.
